implementation_summary.execution_authorization_module: New .orchestrator/execution_authorization.py: derives an immutable execution policy (work_class/repository/environment/resources/action_scope -> policy_digest) for security/hosted/live tasks, builds/verifies a durable pending_authorization hold, verifies a signed MFA-bound grant against a trusted-issuer key set distinct from the dev-bridge packet-source keys, enforces one-shot nonce consumption, and exposes the pure is_execution_authorized query plus reserve/revoke state transitions.
implementation_summary.dispatch_gate: rewrite/dispatch_admission.py TaskIntent gained execution_authorized (default True); evaluate_dispatch_intent denies an unauthorized privileged task with DispatchBlockReason.EXECUTION_AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED before any capacity/health/endpoint check. dispatch_policy.py's evaluate_task_delivery_admission computes this verdict via execution_authorization.is_execution_authorized.
implementation_summary.intake_retirement: dev_bridge_materialize.verify_signed_dev_bridge_packet no longer requires BridgeOperatorAuthorization/mfa_verified for security/hosted/live packets at intake (the former MFA-at-intake rule). The privileged-only packet-identity replay ledger is retained, now keyed by the source's own packet_id instead of an operator nonce that no longer exists.
implementation_summary.pending_hold_materialization: scripts/ai_status.py command_assign attaches execution_authorization.pending_authorization_hold(...) to a brand-new task's metadata when the signed dev_bridge work_class is privileged; an already-materialized task's reassignment/replay path never re-derives or overwrites the frozen record.
implementation_summary.human_ops_cli: New execution-grant-submit / execution-grant-revoke commands (registered in LOCAL_HUMAN_OPS_ACTIONS and TASK_ID_COMMAND_ARG_INDEX) verify a signed grant via EXECUTION_GRANT_JSON against EXECUTION_MFA_ISSUER_PUBLIC_KEYS_JSON, consume its one-shot nonce in a canonical replay ledger, and transition the task to STATE_GRANTED. show <task-id> already surfaces the fully redacted state.
implementation_summary.claim_lease_spend: supervisor.reserve_execution_authorization_for_launch is the authoritative claim/lease-boundary one-shot spend: called immediately before start_worker_for_request's adapter.deliver, under its own exclusive canonical task-state lock (never nested inside the existing shared lock, to avoid a same-process lock-upgrade deadlock), re-verifying and committing STATE_GRANTED -> STATE_RESERVED bound to the exact run id. A cheap in-memory pre-check on the already-loaded dispatch-loop state means a non-privileged task never takes this lock. process_queue treats a failed reserve (ExecutionAuthorizationSpendFailed) as a late-eligibility skip, matching the existing StaleDispatchBeforeLaunch handling.
